title: Biz Insight: Why Palantir's Commercial Revenue Now Outruns Government
description: In Q3 2026 Palantir's U.S. enterprise revenue of $984M passed U.S. government revenue of $953M for the first time. We examine what drove the crossover, the 6% booking growth hiding inside it, the shadow over the government moat, and the Changshin deal.

faqs.question: What does it mean that U.S. commercial revenue passed government revenue?
faqs.answer: In Q3 2026 Palantir earned $984 million from U.S. enterprise customers against $953 million from the U.S. government, a $31 million gap and the first such quarter since the listing. Government revenue grew 96% in the same period, so this is commercial accelerating rather than government stalling.

faqs.question: How is AgentCamp different from an AIP Bootcamp?
faqs.answer: Both are on-site sessions that build something working from the customer's own data within days. A Bootcamp shows an organization new to AIP what it can do; an AgentCamp leans toward building agents that carry out the work. The Changshin partnership was signed after workflows ran on live operating data at an AgentCamp.

faqs.question: How does the Ontology differ from a database schema?
faqs.answer: A schema decides where data lives and in what format. The Ontology sits above that and records the objects, the relationships between them, and the actions that can be taken on them. That is why a model can read that an order is built on a given line and that a delay triggers a specific response.

faqs.question: If bookings rose only 6%, how did revenue rise 96%?
faqs.answer: Revenue is recognized as previously signed contracts burn down, while closed contract value is what was newly signed in the quarter. Q3 total contract value of $2.918 billion was only 6% above last year. Remaining deal value of $13.4 billion keeps near-term revenue intact, but a sustained slowdown in signings shows up in growth a few quarters later.

faqs.question: Why did the stock fall on a strong quarter?
faqs.answer: Shares slid from the day of the print, and most coverage pointed at the deceleration in closed contract value. The November 16 close of $160.39 is about 25% below the all-time high of $212.94 set on October 12. A trailing P/E of 113 also prices in continued acceleration.

faqs.question: What is Michael Burry's case against the stock?
faqs.answer: Burry has kept a short position and disclosed buying March 2027 puts struck at $100. His core argument is that deferred revenue at roughly 32% of revenue makes the model look closer to a consulting firm than a subscription software business. Alex Karp has called the campaign market manipulation.

faqs.question: Where does the government moat actually come from?
faqs.answer: From procurement history and clearances more than from technology. In July 2025 the U.S. Army consolidated 75 contracts into a single enterprise agreement with a $10 billion ceiling, and an August 2026 deputy secretary memo directed up to $244 million in spending through March 2027. Watchdogs criticized that memo for making no mention of competitive procurement.

faqs.question: Is Anthropic a competitor to Palantir?
faqs.answer: It read that way in April 2026, but as of the October product notes, Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5 are offered inside AIP through AWS Bedrock in region-restricted UK environments. The model became a component AIP selects; what Palantir defends is the Ontology and the execution layer.

faqs.question: How does Pebblous DataClinic relate to Palantir?
faqs.answer: Palantir builds an Ontology on the assumption that the data is already in order. DataClinic works upstream of that, diagnosing the quality of unstructured and domain-specific data so it is ready for AI to use. The two are sequential steps, not competing products.
